neighbours.label: ' over' as a preposition after a verb of ruling, overseeing or overlooking (reign over, preside over, tower over, look out over)
fire: Saul was thirty years old when he began to reign over Israel.
The old judge presided over the trial with great patience.
The new skyscraper towers over every other building in the city.
From the balcony she looked out over the harbour at dawn.
The bishop watched over a small flock of rural parishes.
For two centuries the dynasty ruled over a vast empire.
The commander kept watch over the camp through the night.
A hawk hovered over the field, waiting for a mouse.
quiet: Saul was thirty years old when he became the king of Israel.
The old judge led the trial with great patience.
The new skyscraper is taller than every other building in the city.
From the balcony she looked at the harbour at dawn.
The bishop cared for a small flock of rural parishes.
For two centuries the dynasty governed a vast empire.
The commander stayed awake in the camp through the night.
A hawk circled high above the field, waiting for a mouse.

notes: card: ' over' x32 of the top 32, mostly reigned/presided/towered/looked out over. Near misses keep the verbs with other prepositions or none.
